task_instance: Generate a complete design token system from a brand color (#0066CC, 'modern' style) covering colors (10-step scales for primary/secondary/neutral plus semantic colors with WCAG contrast text), typography (1.25x type scale), spacing (8pt grid), borders, shadows, animation, breakpoints and z-index; export it as JSON, CSS custom properties, and SCSS variables, validate the numbers against the WCAG/type-scale formulas in the skill doc, and wire the CSS output into a small demo HTML page as a developer-handoff check.
blocker_detail: The skill package as provided under benchmark/ce_sources_div/.../ui-design-system/ contained only SKILL.md and LICENSE -- the scripts/design_token_generator.py and references/*.md files it documents were not present. This was not a runtime limitation, so I reimplemented the generator directly from the algorithm/tables specified in SKILL.md (HSV-based color scale table, 1.25x typographic ratio, 8pt spacing grid, WCAG relative-luminance contrast formula) rather than treating it as a blocker.
evidence: Wrote design_token_generator.py in the work directory implementing the SKILL.md algorithm. Ran: `python3 design_token_generator.py "#0066CC" modern json > design-tokens.json`, `... css > design-tokens.css`, `... scss > _design-tokens.scss`, and `... summary`. Verified: (1) all 9 token categories present (colors, typography, spacing, borders, shadows, animation, breakpoints, zIndex, plus accessibility) via `json.load` + key check; (2) typography scale matches SKILL.md's table exactly: xs=10px sm=13px base=16px lg=20px xl=25px 2xl=31px 3xl=39px 4xl=49px 5xl=61px; (3) WCAG contrast formula verified against known reference value (white vs black = 21.0:1, the correct WCAG maximum); (4) primary-500 (#3D85CC) on black/white text scored as AA-compliant (5.43:1, both wcagAA_normalText and wcagAA_largeText true); (5) CSS output syntax-checked programmatically (every declaration line ends in ';', wrapped in :root{}); (6) tested across styles (classic, playful) and formats without errors; (7) built demo.html that links design-tokens.css and consumes the actual generated custom-property names (--colors-primary-500, --spacing-scale-16, --borders-radius-default, --shadows-md, --shadows-sm, --borders-radius-lg) confirming the exported tokens are consumable by a real stylesheet. Files produced in work directory: design_token_generator.py, design-tokens.json, design-tokens.css, _design-tokens.scss, demo.html, result.json. No network, credentials, or connector/MCP tools were needed or used.
